comment: Machine-readable shape of DECISIONS.json at skill version 2.0.0-alpha.7. Read this when a DECISIONS.json records a different skill_version than the installed skill: there is no backwards compatibility, so the agent holding the file upgrades it or rewrites it.

title.note: the question, stated as a question

status.note: the lifecycle is open -> decided -> implemented; closed/dropped/obsolete can withdraw a question from any of those three, with or without ever implementing it

branch.note: the git branch the question was raised on, as context -- not a filter key other fields key off

context.note: why the question was raised, and what the agent stubbed or assumed while it stayed open

chosen.note: the letter the user picked, once decided

resolution.note: set when the question is implemented (what was done) or closed (why it was withdrawn)

invariants: every option has a distinct letter
chosen, when set, names one of the question's own options
a question only reaches implemented from decided

2.0.0-alpha.6.describes: A question register written by skill version 2.0.0-alpha.6.
steps: rjq '.skill_version = "2.0.0-alpha.7"' DECISIONS.json > DECISIONS.json.tmp && mv DECISIONS.json.tmp DECISIONS.json

2.0.0-alpha.5.describes: A question register written by skill version 2.0.0-alpha.5.
steps: rjq '.skill_version = "2.0.0-alpha.7"' DECISIONS.json > DECISIONS.json.tmp && mv DECISIONS.json.tmp DECISIONS.json

2.0.0-alpha.4.describes: A question register written by skill version 2.0.0-alpha.4, whose Status enum had `answered` instead of `decided` and no `implemented` state at all.
2.0.0-alpha.4.loses: an answered-but-not-closed question cannot be renamed in place by a mechanical recipe, because its answer (chosen) and context are worth a human or agent's own re-filing rather than a blind field rewrite -- re-raise it with `decisions add`, carrying its old title, options, priority and context across, then `decisions answer` it again with its old chosen letter. An already-closed, dropped or obsolete entry needs nothing: those status names are unchanged, and this version's own `decisions` binary archives them exactly as the previous one did.
steps: Read the backup this upgrade produced and find every entry with status "answered".
For each: decisions add --title "..." --option a:... --option b:... --priority <urgent|high|normal|low|someday> --context "..." (carrying the old entry's own fields)
Everything else in the register (open, closed, dropped, obsolete entries) is carried forward automatically; only answered entries need this manual step.

if_no_schema_for_a_version: Rewrite the file by hand against the closest schema.*.json this skill ships, correcting field by field; do not guess at an intermediate shape.
